# Command-line reference

**For:** operators. Every command and option of the `ferroehr` binary,
as `ferroehr <command> --help` prints it. The guides to the commands are
on [CLI & production checklist](../installation/config-cli.md).

<!-- toc -->

## `ferroehr`

```text
openEHR-conformant CDR server

Usage: ferroehr [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  serve          Serves until the process is asked to stop
  config         Works on the configuration
  healthcheck    Asks the server running beside this process whether it is ready, and exits 0 only when it is
  db             Database schema utilities (apply or verify the migrations, or erase the instance), then exit
  usage-report   The usage report to `FerroPULSE`: print the report this instance would send, without sending it
  definitions    The definition store: `load` templates from files before `serve`
  access-log     The access log: seal a checkpoint, verify, export and import
  audit-chain    The system chain, the records outside the access log: seal its head and verify it
  party-binding  The party binding side table: `refill` it after a mapping change
  pmir           The PMIR feed messages the consumer refused: list, retry or settle them
  report         Write a redacted report of what this deployment runs (build, features, specification pins, migration level, posture, licence, manufacturer and configuration), the file a complaint or an incident report attaches
  help           Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --config <PATH>
          The TOML configuration file; unset, the product's `_CONFIG` variable names it

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          One configuration key set over the file and the environment, as `key=value`; repeatable

  -h, --help
          Print help

  -V, --version
          Print version
```

## `ferroehr db`

```text
Database schema utilities (apply or verify the migrations, or erase the instance), then exit

Usage: ferroehr db [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  migrate      Apply the embedded migrations and exit; the DSN must hold DDL rights
  verify       Verify, without issuing any DDL, that the database carries exactly this build's migrations; exit 0 when it does, 1 otherwise
  erase        Permanently erase every piece of data and every setting this instance stores: the multimedia blobs, then every schema the migrations create
  sweep-blobs  Delete every multimedia blob no stored version references and that is older than `[record.multimedia] orphan_grace`: the blobs commits that failed after their upload left behind

          Print help
```

## `ferroehr db erase`

```text
Permanently erase every piece of data and every setting this instance stores: the multimedia blobs, then every schema the migrations create.

Without `--confirm` it erases nothing: it prints what it would erase and the value `--confirm` must carry, and exits 1. Run it with every server stopped; the DSN must own the schemas.

Usage: ferroehr db erase [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --config <PATH>
          The TOML configuration file; unset, the product's `_CONFIG` variable names it

      --confirm <INSTANCE>
          The instance to erase, as the run without `--confirm` prints it: the stored instance id, or the clinical database's name when the database stores no instance id

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          One configuration key set over the file and the environment, as `key=value`; repeatable

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `ferroehr db sweep-blobs`

```text
Delete every multimedia blob no stored version references and that is older than `[record.multimedia] orphan_grace`: the blobs commits that failed after their upload left behind.

Without `--apply` it deletes nothing and prints what it would delete. It can run while servers serve: a blob younger than the grace period is always kept.

Usage: ferroehr db sweep-blobs [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --apply
          Delete the orphans instead of listing them

      --config <PATH>
          The TOML configuration file; unset, the product's `_CONFIG` variable names it

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          One configuration key set over the file and the environment, as `key=value`; repeatable

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `ferroehr definitions`

```text
The definition store: `load` templates from files before `serve`

Usage: ferroehr definitions [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  load  Store each file in the definition store, in the order given, with the validation and versioning of the REST upload, then exit.           The TOML configuration file; unset, the product's `_CONFIG` variable names it
```

```text
      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          One configuration key set over the file and the environment, as `key=value`; repeatable

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `ferroehr access-log`

```text
The access log: seal a checkpoint, verify, export and import

Usage: ferroehr access-log [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  checkpoint  Print the checkpoint of the head of the access log, sealing it with the keyring's key when no append sealed it
  verify      Verify the access log against its newest checkpoint, or the one in `--checkpoint`, and print every finding. Exits non-zero when the log does not verify

  import      Import an EHR's access log another system exported, verified against its checkpoint and `[audit.access_log] trusted_key_files`, and record the import as an entry of this system's log
  help        Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --config <PATH>
          The TOML configuration file; unset, the product's `_CONFIG` variable names it

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          One configuration key set over the file and the environment, as `key=value`; repeatable

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `ferroehr party-binding`

```text
The party binding side table: `refill` it after a mapping change

Usage: ferroehr party-binding [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  refill  Rebuild the binding side table, the policy grants included, from the party versions under the configured mapping and store its digest. Run it with every replica stopped: it refuses while a replica's lease is live. A key issuer added or removed needs no refill: the running replicas fill and retire its key space themselves. With no mapping configured it rebuilds the policy grants alone. It then rebuilds the `EHR_ACCESS` projection from every EHR's current `EHR_ACCESS` version
  check   Report, from the party versions and writing nothing, what binding will make of them: the keys per issuer, duplicates, inactive and abandoned persons, the provisional persons just-in-time creation left incomplete for longer than `[authz.party_binding] provisional_report_after`, key-bearing persons with no professional `ROLE`, the mapped Basic users, and the committer that introduced each key. It exits non-zero on a duplicate, a missing person or a key whose committer fails the provenance rule
  adopt   Give each listed `PERSON` a professional `ROLE` of the mapping's role template, in one demographic CONTRIBUTION committed by the first administrator named, with one access record per adopted `PERSON`. It refuses, naming them, the `PERSON`s whose key fails the provenance rule of `check`
  grant   Grant an operation of the `openehr_access` terminology to a client, on the operator's authority: an `AGENT` carrying the client identifier, unless an `ACTOR` names the client already, and a `ROLE` it performs whose capability grants the operation with the scope elements given. It is the first grant of a new deployment, such as the `scim_provision` of the client that provisions the administrators; every later grant is an administrator's write through the Demographic API. A client that holds the operation already gets nothing. With `--basic-user`, the `ROLE` is performed by the `PERSON` the Basic user binds to, such as the `hold_scopes` of a development lane's users
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --config <PATH>
          The TOML configuration file; unset, the product's `_CONFIG` variable names it

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          One configuration key set over the file and the environment, as `key=value`; repeatable

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `ferroehr party-binding check`

```text
Report, from the party versions and writing nothing, what binding will make of them: the keys per issuer, duplicates, inactive and abandoned persons, the provisional persons just-in-time creation left incomplete for longer than `[authz.party_binding] provisional_report_after`, key-bearing persons with no professional `ROLE`, the mapped Basic users, and the committer that introduced each key. It exits non-zero on a duplicate, a missing person or a key whose committer fails the provenance rule

Usage: ferroehr party-binding check [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --admin <PARTY_ID>
          An administrator, named by the container id of its `PERSON`: a key its commit introduced passes the provenance rule

      --config <PATH>
          The TOML configuration file; unset, the product's `_CONFIG` variable names it

      --admin-key <ISSUER> <KEY>
          An administrator, named by the `identifier_issuer` and value of a binding key its `PERSON` carries

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          One configuration key set over the file and the environment, as `key=value`; repeatable

      --migration <COMMITTER_NAME>
          The committer name of a migration the operator declares: a key its commit introduced passes the provenance rule

      --expected <FILE>
          The identity provider's assigned users, one login identifier per line: every one with no `PERSON` is listed

      --expected-issuer <ISSUER>
          The `identifier_issuer` the `--expected` logins are keys of; needed when more than one `[auth.issuer.<name>.party]` table is configured

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

```text

      --set <KEY=VALUE>

      --migration <COMMITTER_NAME>
```

## `ferroehr party-binding grant`

```text
Grant an operation of the `openehr_access` terminology to a client, on the operator's authority: an `AGENT` carrying the client identifier, unless an `ACTOR` names the client already, and a `ROLE` it performs whose capability grants the operation with the scope elements given. It is the first grant of a new deployment, such as the `scim_provision` of the client that provisions the administrators; every later grant is an administrator's write through the Demographic API. A client that holds the operation already gets nothing. With `--basic-user`, the `ROLE` is performed by the `PERSON` the Basic user binds to, such as the `hold_scopes` of a development lane's users

Usage: ferroehr party-binding grant [OPTIONS] --operation <CODE>

Options:
      --config <PATH>
          The TOML configuration file; unset, the product's `_CONFIG` variable names it

      --issuer <ISSUER>
          The issuer of the client's tokens

      --client-id <CLIENT_ID>
          The client's OAuth 2.0 `client_id`

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          One configuration key set over the file and the environment, as `key=value`; repeatable

      --basic-user <USER>
          The Basic user of `[[auth.basic.users]]` whose `PERSON` is granted the operation, found by the binding key `[[authz.party_binding.basic_user]]` maps it by, in place of a client

      --operation <CODE>
          The operation's code, such as `scim_provision`

      --element <CODE=TEXT>
          A scope element of the grant, its code of the draft access terminology and the text it names, such as `binding_issuer=urn:example:login`

      --provider-issuer <ISSUER>
          The issuer of a `provider` element's `DV_IDENTIFIER`, paired in order with `--provider-id`: a provider whose care relationships and memberships a `write_care_relationship` grant writes

      --provider-id <ID>
          The id of a `provider` element's `DV_IDENTIFIER`, paired in order with `--provider-issuer`

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `ferroehr pmir`

```text
The PMIR feed messages the consumer refused: list, retry or settle them

Usage: ferroehr pmir [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  list    Print the refused messages still to retry or settle, oldest first, as JSON: each with its refusal code, receipt and refusal time, attempts, the Registry's identities it names and the `PERSON`s it keeps split, as counts. No identifier value is printed
  retry   Put a refused message back at its arrival position once its cause is fixed, such as a `[[pix.identifier_domain]]` entry or a grant added; a running replica applies it next. Refused when a message received after it that names one of its identities has applied
  settle  Close a refused message without applying it: `discard` keeps its splits, `lift-splits` removes them so its identifiers and record subjects resolve as before the message. A discarded message may still have its splits lifted
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --config <PATH>
          The TOML configuration file; unset, the product's `_CONFIG` variable names it

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          One configuration key set over the file and the environment, as `key=value`; repeatable

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `ferroehr pmir settle`

```text

Arguments:
  <MESSAGE_ID>
          The message's `MessageHeader.id`

Options:
      --config <PATH>
          The TOML configuration file; unset, the product's `_CONFIG` variable names it

      --decision <DECISION>
          `discard` or `lift-splits`

      --reason <TEXT>

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          One configuration key set over the file and the environment, as `key=value`; repeatable

      --operator <NAME>
          The operator the row and the access record name

  -h, --help
          Print help
```
